title: Driventic refurbs London old-timer electric double-decker bus drivetrains
summary: In London, 28 aging electric double-deckers are being comprehensively refurbished. The electric old-timers will receive new batteries and electric drives. The latter are being supplied by the German drivetrain specialist Driventic. After modernization, the electric double-deckers are set to return to service with the transport company Metroline.

title: Orders open for the Genesis GV90 in South Korea
summary: Genesis is opening order books in South Korea for the GV90, its electric flagship. The highlight of the lineup is the four-seat Neolun variant, featuring all available equipment options, including the VIP package and underfloor heating, starting at approximately €165,600. The market launch in Europe is planned for the first half of 2027.

title: China’s electric car exports surge by 140 Per Cent
summary: Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids manufactured in China are increasingly becoming an export hit for the People's Republic: In October alone, 606,000 plug-in vehicles were exported from the country — an increase of 140%. In contrast, domestic sales in China declined by 8.6%.

title: Kia invests billions in electric and PBV Centre
summary: Kia plans to gradually transform the Autoland Gwangju plant into a modern hub for electric and autonomous vehicles by 2029, investing billions. The goal is to establish an industrial ecosystem for the development of modular electric vehicles, which Kia calls PBV - standing for "platform beyond vehicle" and simultaneously the anacronym for Purpose Built Vehicles (PBVs), in collaboration with the region and local universities.

title: Tozero announces first delivery of recycled lithium carbonate to customers
summary: The German lithium-ion battery recycling startup Tozero has delivered its first recycled lithium carbonate to an industrial customer, Botz GmbH. The material was produced at Tozero's new demonstration plant in the Gendorf Chemical Park near Munich.

title: German study compares electric motors from China, Europe and the USA
summary: Researchers at Germany's renown RWTH Aachen University examined 115 electric motors from 80 electric vehicles. They found that drivetrains from China, Europe, and the USA differ little in their basic design but vary in materials and individual construction details.

title: BYD combines solar arrays, energy storage and megawatt charging
summary: BYD has unveiled a charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that combines photovoltaics, battery storage, FLASH Charging, and a charging robot. According to CarNewsChina, the system achieved a charging power of 1,000 kW during a demonstration.

title: Mercedes discontinues EQE, EQE SUV and EQS SUV
summary: The EQE sedan, EQE SUV, and EQS SUV are no longer individually configurable at Mercedes-Benz. This leaves only the EQS sedan remaining from the four large electric models based on the EVA-II platform, while a fully electric E-Class as an EQE alternative has already been announced for 2027.

title: California reopens $55m funding programme for electric school buses
summary: California has reopened its Zero-Emission School Bus and Infrastructure (ZESBI) incentive programme, with at least $55 million in state funding available to help school districts purchase electric school buses and install the associated charging infrastrcture.

title: India: ChargeZone announces 1,000 new DC fast-charging sites
summary: Indian EV charging service provider ChargeZone has announced plans to deploy DC fast chargers across 1,000 new locations in the country. The company says these chargers will serve both passenger and commercial electric vehicles.

title: Zenobe to finance 169 electric buses for Transport UK in London
summary: Zenobē has agreed to finance 169 battery-electric buses for Transport UK, alongside the development of charging infrastructure at four of the operator's London depots. The deal extends an existing partnership between the two companies and supports Transport UK's ambition to fully electrify its London bus fleet by 2030.

title: Infineon processes SiC on 300 mm wafers for the first time
summary: Infineon has produced the first functional SiC power devices on 300-millimeter wafers. The larger wafer diameter is intended to make production more efficient and, in the long term, improve supply for applications including EVs and charging infrastructure.

title: Faulty software? Waymo faces potential new recall
summary: The US traffic safety authority NHTSA has launched a new investigation into Alphabet's subsidiary Waymo after its driverless taxis repeatedly passed stopped school buses in violation of regulations. An investigation is now exploring why a software update rolled out at the end of 2025 failed to prevent these dangerous violations.

title: Kia reveals UK prices for PV5 Chassis and high-roof electric van
summary: Two new additions to Kia's PV5 electric van range, the Chassis and the high-roof Cargo L2/H2, are expected to be available from £25,605 and £27,355 respectively - once they qualify for the UK's Zero Emission Van Grant (ZEVG). Both models are now available to order, with first deliveries of the Chassis expected in Q1 2027.

title: Xpeng launches range-extender SUVs in 11 Middle Eastern and African markets
summary: Xpeng has opened pre-orders for its flagship GX and G9L SUVs in 11 countries across the MEA region. The two models are being introduced in a shared launch across ten markets, with the GX also launching in Egypt and the G9L in Ghana.

title: Pulsa to open private wallboxes for EV drivers
summary: With Pulsa, private wallboxes can be temporarily made accessible to other EV drivers. Three weeks after its launch, the platform has reported 250 registrations.

title: Volvo Penta and Ammann develop all-electric road paver
summary: Swiss construction machinery manufacturer Ammann, together with drive specialist Volvo Penta, has developed a fully electric road paver. The eABG 4820 is designed to combine the performance of conventional diesel machines with locally emission-free operation.

title: CATL explores lithium-air batteries as a long-term research focus
summary: CATL is considering lithium-air batteries as a long-term research option. The technology theoretically promises a significantly higher energy density than today's lithium-ion batteries. However, it is still far from market-ready vehicle batteries or a range of 2,000 km.

title: Polestar’s design strategy: Formula 2030 showcar sets the direction
summary: Polestar unveils the Formula 2030 concept car, showcasing the brand's future design direction. Formula 2030 is the first study under the leadership of Chief Designer Philipp Römers, who took up the position in mid-2024. As a four-door sports car, the show car is intended to emphasize that performance remains at the heart of the brand.

title: BYD considers building a battery factory in Portugal
summary: BYD is reportedly considering building a battery factory in Portugal - potentially at the former Galp refinery in Matosinhos near Porto. It remains unclear whether battery cells or complete battery systems would be manufactured there. Such a battery factory would align well with a potential BYD car factory in Spain.

title: VW hints at SSP model production at Martorell Seat plant
summary: In an internal report on future collective bargaining strategy, Volkswagen has also indicated that it will "probably assign a platform and products" to the Seat plant in Martorell (Spain). This could refer to the SSP, which will underpin the electric successors to the Cupra Leon and Formentor.

title: Mercedes eCitaro to switch to a dedicated electric platform from 2028
summary: Daimler Buses has announced the second generation eCitaro. From 2028, the electric city bus will be based on a dedicated electric platform, utilise LFP batteries – and even handle some intercity routes. We attended the presentation of the near-series prototype in Munich.

title: Chargebyte launches more robust control unit for megawatt charging stations
summary: With the new Charge Control Y, Chargebyte now offers a high-load charging controller for megawatt charging in heavy-duty transport. The IP65-protected control unit is designed to reliably protect charging stations in depots, ports, and logistics centers from extreme weather and high-voltage faults.

title: Renault opens UK pre-orders for Trafic E-Tech electric from £38,000
summary: UK customers can now place pre-orders for the new Trafic E-Tech electric van, which was first presented by Renault in November 2025. Prices start from £38,000 ex. VAT, with the first customer deliveries scheduled for Q2 of 2027.

title: Perth’s largest electric bus depot opens as Transperth fleet surpasses 200 vehicles
summary: Western Australia's largest electric bus depot has opened in Bayswater, Perth. The new facility is equipped with 65 dual chargers and two single chargers, and can initially accommodate 132 electric buses - with scope for up to 180 long term.

title: Greenspot and Kempower to build 30 fast-charging sites in France
summary: Greenspot plans to install Kempower fast-charging infrastructure at 30 retail locations in France by the end of 2027. Each site will feature four charging points powered by a central 200 kW unit.

title: Wien Energie expands charging network across Austria following Ella acquisition
summary: Following the acquisition of Ella GmbH & Co KG, Austrian energy provider Wien Energie has now fully taken over 500 publicly accessible charging points in Lower Austria, Upper Austria, and Burgenland - and, following a multi-month transition phase, integrated them into its charging network.

title: Norway: Ionity halts Ekoenergetyka pilot – and installs Huawei chargers for first time
summary: At the end of 2025, Ionity opened its first charging park in Elverum, Norway - which features the so-called Shared Power technology by Ekoenergetyka. However, the pilot failed. Since then, Ionity has removed the charging stations and replaced them with new ones from Huawei. It marks the first time that Ionity will work with Huawei.

title: Egypt’s first electric car: Dongfeng Mage EV rolls off the production line
summary: Egypt has launched production of its first locally manufactured electric car, marking the beginning of a new e-mobility offensive. The Dongfeng Mage EV is being built in the state-owned El Nasr Automotive workshops. Egypt aims to produce up to 100,000 electric vehicles annually by 2032.

title: 60 driverless electric haul trucks operating at 5,400 metres above sea level
summary: In China’s Zhibula copper mine, 60 battery-electric dump trucks are now operating fully autonomously at an altitude of over 5,400 meters. EACON Mining and Julong Copper have gradually introduced driverless operations since 2025, achieving what they claim is a unique deployment in high-altitude mining.
